rows.subtype: Approach: packing the finished work in the bag straight away [Action]
rows.description: Once the last page is done, a girl puts the notebooks in her school bag immediately. This avoids the morning panic of remembering that the homework is somewhere on the study table.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: counting days left and dividing the chapters [Thinking]
rows.description: A child with a Social Studies test in four days counts six chapters and plans one and a half chapters a day. Dividing the big task into daily pieces makes it feel doable.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: reading the chapter again and again [Action]
rows.description: A boy reads his science chapter three times, highlighting nothing. The words look familiar, so he feels ready, though he has only recognised the text and not tried to recall it.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: feeling ready because the page looks familiar [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl closes the book and thinks she knows photosynthesis. When her mother asks her to explain it, she cannot say the steps, showing that familiarity is not the same as knowing.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: making questions and answering from memory [Thinking]
rows.description: A child turns each heading into a question, such as Why do we have seasons, and answers aloud with the book closed. Checking wrong answers tells him exactly what to study again.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: teaching the chapter to a younger sibling or toy [Action]
rows.description: A girl explains the water cycle to her little brother using a steel glass and steam from a kettle held safely by her mother. Where she stumbles is where she has not understood.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: practising old test papers under time [Action]
rows.description: A boy solves last year's maths paper at the dining table with a clock, then checks answers. He learns he spends too long on one question and decides to skip and return.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: skipping the boring chapter and hoping it will not come [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl leaves out the Civics chapter because she dislikes it and thinks the teacher will not ask from it. The paper has an eight-mark question on it, and she loses easy marks.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning

rows.subtype: Approach: switching tactics after a bad practice score [Revision]
rows.description: After scoring only 5 out of 10 in her own quiz, a child notices that reading alone is not working. She switches to writing key points on cards and quizzing herself, and her next score rises.

rows.subtype: Approach: studying with a friend and swapping questions [Action]
rows.description: Two classmates meet after school and each writes five questions for the other. Their questions cover different parts of the chapter, and hearing each other's explanations fills small gaps.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning
